correctness.rationale: The 16-survivor-subset enumeration of the nonplane rooted four-leaf caterpillar and balanced fork supplies the stated polynomial PGF difference. Grafting a common new root and singleton multiplies the PGF difference by qz+(1-q)z^2, since contributions from all-extinct old leaves cancel. Induction gives the all-n factorization, its derivative at z=1 gives q²(1-q), and summing coefficient degrees >=n-1 gives q^(n-2)(1-q)((n-2)q-(n-4)). Since 2-,3-leaf trees are unique and the only 4-leaf ordering agrees, discordance first occurs at n=5 with q<1/3. Independently enumerated rooted descendant-edge masks and exact integer q-polynomials for n=4..8; these finite tests corroborate the PGF identities and do not replace induction.
residual_risks: Only rooted PD with 2n-2 unit edges and no root stem; the model is intentionally non-ultrametric and relies on independence of extinctions.

value.rationale: The probability of retaining half the original phylogenetic diversity is an interpretable risk quantity distinct from expectation. Five taxa as sharp first mean-risk discordance and a closed crossover q=(n-4)/(n-2) for every larger n give a useful exact structural witness. This is not an arbitrary instance or a downstream theorem requirement.
